openQuestions: Which tokenization, prompting, model, judge, and evaluation changes improve readability without weakening privacy or exact fidelity?

resolvedQuestions.question: What currently limits rewrite quality?
resolvedQuestions.answer: Broad protection creates opaque-token copying burden, the wire prompt has no token-aware rubric or examples, and the semantic layer is a reject-only veto.

resolvedQuestions.question: Which prompt/profile and provider controls are admissible for quality experiments?
resolvedQuestions.answer: The prompt contract is versioned but has no examples or token rubric; DeepSeek temperature/thinking controls remain unknown and the compiler fails closed until fresh confirmed evidence exists.

resolvedQuestions.question: Is the meaning-preservation judge wired into provider/runtime rendering?
resolvedQuestions.answer: No in-package production composition call was found. The validator exposes an opt-in reject-only judge, but the evaluation veto disables it and runtime presentation consumes an already validated render decision.

resolvedQuestions.question: Which architecture best balances readability and safety?
resolvedQuestions.answer: Typed assembly supports deterministic formatting for known event classes, but raw-text references limit universal templates. Retain local protection/restoration and add a hybrid deterministic skeleton plus bounded prose slots.

resolvedQuestions.question: Does projection earn its complexity over deterministic formatting, and which user journeys justify it?
resolvedQuestions.answer: Conditionally: multi-sentence, technical, user-facing warnings, caveats, consequences, and recovery explanations can justify a deterministic-first hybrid; short or structured messages should remain deterministic/native. Quality efficacy and net user benefit still require a fixed-corpus human comparison.

keyFindings.title: Opaque protected tokens consume readability budget
keyFindings.summary: A 95-character representative sentence produced five 48-character opaque tokens and a 270-character encoded message.

keyFindings.title: Meaning judge is opt-in and reject-only
keyFindings.summary: The validator calls a judge only in required mode and has no candidate ranking or readability score.

keyFindings.title: Inline ranges are not coalesced
keyFindings.summary: Each non-overlapping path, flag, identifier, or number receives a separate opaque token; a read-only probe measured 33 characters to 157 with three spans and 36 to 204 with four spans.

keyFindings.title: Prompt profiles have no token-aware examples
keyFindings.summary: The profile carries one system instruction and inference controls but no few-shot examples, token inventory, or readability rubric.

keyFindings.title: DeepSeek quality controls are unconfirmed
keyFindings.summary: The DeepSeek preset and reference fixture mark temperature/thinking support unknown, so the control compiler returns unsupported-control before transport rather than silently assuming the setting applied.

keyFindings.title: Optional meaning judge is not composed into rendering
keyFindings.summary: Provider execution returns a candidate and runtime presentation consumes a validation result; no production source call connects them through the optional judge.

keyFindings.title: Judge seam receives restored protected values
keyFindings.summary: When required, the injected reject-only judge sees decoded source text and restored candidate text, so a hosted judge would be a separate privacy egress.

keyFindings.title: Offline proxy review is provisional evidence
keyFindings.summary: Masked proxy scores cover meaning-preservation and style dimensions, but release readiness requires non-provisional human-certifiable evidence.

keyFindings.title: Typed assembly can carry a deterministic skeleton
keyFindings.summary: Runtime-neutral event kinds, lifecycle, order domains, canonical references, and exact-original assembly already form a safe local foundation for structured formatting.

keyFindings.title: Current payloads limit universal templates
keyFindings.summary: Assistant/tool payloads in the Codex adapter commonly point to canonical text IDs rather than exposing typed semantic fields, so arbitrary prose still needs a model or richer upstream contracts.

keyFindings.title: Hybrid skeleton plus prose slots fits the boundaries
keyFindings.summary: A deterministic technical skeleton with bounded protected prose slots reduces whole-message marker burden while preserving local restoration and tiered rendering.

keyFindings.title: Deterministic formatting should own short and structured messages
keyFindings.summary: Typed lifecycle, status, command/result, and other short messages have little incremental readability value from a model route and should default to native or deterministic formatting.

keyFindings.title: Complex user-facing warnings and recovery prose are the high-value slice
keyFindings.summary: Projection is most plausibly valuable for multi-sentence explanations that combine progress, caveats, consequences, or next steps, subject to measurement against a deterministic baseline.

keyFindings.title: Privacy, evidence, and operational costs set a high adoption bar
keyFindings.summary: Privacy-before-transport, fresh capability facts, human release evidence, latency, provider cost, rejection, fallback, and timeout measures must be weighed against user benefit.

keyFindings.title: Safe-native rollout and provider-free rollback bound risk
keyFindings.summary: Append/sidecar presentation and OriginalOnlyEmergencyMode allow a narrow experiment without suppressing the original or requiring a provider during rollback.

ruledOutDirections.reason: Exact ordered restoration is the fail-closed privacy/fidelity boundary.

ruledOutDirections.direction: Remove protection categories to improve prose
ruledOutDirections.reason: It would expose values currently kept outside the provider request; use grouping or wire aliases instead and keep local canonical bytes.

ruledOutDirections.direction: Use offline proxy reviewer as runtime meaning judge
ruledOutDirections.reason: Its contract is comparative masked scoring with provisional evidence, not reject-only candidate validation.

ruledOutDirections.direction: Use semantic diff as the sole renderer
ruledOutDirections.reason: The semantic comparator is a deterministic rejection/diagnostic layer and cannot generate clearer prose.
Short and structured output has little incremental readability value while every model route adds latency, provider, validation, and fallback cost.

ruledOutDirections.direction: Use hosted routing as the default quality upgrade
ruledOutDirections.reason: Hosted routing requires explicit consent and fresh privacy facts, and no source-backed provider or tier quality advantage has been established.

nextFocus: No further loop; future work is the fixed-corpus quality and human non-inferiority validation described in research.md.
